metadata.summary: The ISIC Archive and its annual challenges provide the largest publicly available collection of dermoscopic images of skin lesions for skin cancer analysis. ISIC 2024 (SLICE-3D) released 401,059 training images (crops from 3D total-body photography) from 1,042 patients for melanoma classification. Historical challenges (e.g., 2020) contributed 33,126 DICOM images and incorporated prior datasets including HAM10000.
metadata.purpose: Skin cancer classification and segmentation for academic challenge participation.

papers.title: ISIC 2024 / Historical: The International Skin Imaging Collaboration skin lesion analysis challenges

ethics.privacy_measures: Images are de-identified; no protected health information retained.
ethics.legal_compliance: Complies with GDPR and HIPAA de-identification standards per ISIC governance documentation.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.

known_limitations: Underrepresentation of pediatric and elderly populations.
Geographic bias toward high-resource countries with dermatology infrastructure.
Label noise due to inter-rater variability and diagnostic evolution.
Limited representation of skin of color in earlier releases (e.g., pre-2024).
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Cropping from 3D total-body photography (2024); integration of prior datasets (e.g., HAM10000) with harmonized labeling.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Predominantly adult, light-skin-tone, high-resource-country populations; limited diversity in age, ethnicity, and geography.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Melanoma and nevus dominate; rarer lesions (e.g., dermatofibroma, vascular lesions) are underrepresented.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Performance may degrade on populations with darker skin tones, pediatric/elderly patients, or lesions imaged outside standardized dermoscopic protocols.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Subgroup coverage by skin tone, age, and geography is uneven and incompletely documented.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic metadata (age, sex, ethnicity) is largely missing or inconsistently reported across historical releases.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Direct clinical deployment without validation; commercial use without explicit permission.

data_origin.selection_rationale: International multi-site contributors; selected to support skin cancer classification and segmentation challenges.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Multi-site aggregation; includes crops from 3D total-body photography (2024) and legacy DICOM dermoscopic images (e.g., 2020, HAM10000).

population.target_population: Patients with skin lesions undergoing dermoscopic imaging.
population.inclusion_criteria: Skin lesion images acquired via dermoscopy or 3D total-body photography.
population.missing_groups: Pediatric and elderly populations are underrepresented; exact proportions not reported.

annotation.annotation_method: Expert dermatologist labeling; some labels derived from clinical reports or prior curated datasets (e.g., HAM10000).
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels sourced from clinical diagnosis, expert review, and prior public datasets (e.g., HAM10000); known label noise exists due to inter-rater variability and evolving diagnostic criteria.
annotation.label_noise_description: Inter-rater variability and diagnostic uncertainty in borderline lesions; some historical labels may not reflect current consensus.
